incidents.vector: Zero-click mobile spyware (NSO Group Pegasus) delivered to the target's phone via crafted messages.
incidents.impact: Citizen Lab confirmed a Greek journalist and former MEP who sat on the European Parliament committee investigating spyware abuse was himself infected with Pegasus twice, in Oct 2022 and Mar 2023, during the panel's most sensitive work — a likely breach of parliamentary privilege.

incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion; initial access method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: One of Taiwan's largest mobile operators was breached and is being extorted by a newly launched ransomware group; the carrier says its mobile-payments platform was unaffected and Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs has opened an investigation.

incidents.vector: Undisclosed network intrusion occurring between March and April 2026.
incidents.impact: Kubota's North American division disclosed a breach that exposed employee information; no group has claimed responsibility.

incidents.victim: Organizations running internet-exposed Fortinet FortiGate firewalls
incidents.vector: Internet-wide password spraying and a privilege-escalation flaw turned FortiGate firewalls into credential stealers via a Go-based sniffer, with config-file credential theft and admin persistence; the group is also exploiting an unpatched Nextcloud zero-day.
incidents.impact: The 'FortiBleed' access-broker operation compromised thousands of FortiGate devices (sniffer still on ~12,000; credentials for 30,000+) and is now feeding that access to ransomware crews — researchers confirmed at least 12 ransomware deployments and hundreds of encrypted endpoints, with full domain-admin compromise on 354 targets.

incidents.victim: Consumer smart TVs and streaming boxes (2M+ devices worldwide)
incidents.vector: Malicious SDKs hidden in TV-box and smart-TV apps silently enrolled home devices as always-on residential-proxy exit nodes.
incidents.impact: Google, the FBI and Lumen coordinated a takedown of the NetNut/Popa residential-proxy network, seizing hundreds of domains and cutting the proxy pool by millions of devices; the service had been used by 316 distinct threat-actor clusters, including criminal and espionage groups, for password spraying and traffic obfuscation.

incidents.victim: Small businesses across the US, Europe, Asia and the Middle East
incidents.industry: Cross-sector (SMBs: pharma, food/agriculture, tech, media, legal)
incidents.vector: Phishing emails impersonating Interpol claim the recipient is under criminal investigation and lure victims into opening a password-protected archive that delivers ransomware disguised as video evidence.
incidents.impact: An emerging low-sophistication ransomware campaign is hitting small businesses that assume they are 'too small' to target; ransom amounts are negotiated per-victim over the Tox messaging platform based on perceived ability to pay.

incidents.victim: Oracle E-Business Suite customers (~950 exposed instances, majority in the US)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of CVE-2026-46817, a critical (CVSS 9.8) low-complexity flaw in the payments-processing feature of Oracle E-Business Suite.
incidents.impact: Researchers observed the first in-the-wild exploitation from a single IP before any public proof-of-concept, likely reconnaissance and weaponization ahead of a broader campaign against a widely deployed business-application suite that criminal extortion crews have targeted en masse before.

incidents.victim: Luxury jewelry retailer and a US insurance company
incidents.vector: Voice calls to corporate IT help desks requesting MFA and password resets compromised employee accounts within hours, followed by tunneling tools for persistent access.
incidents.impact: A 19-year-old dual US-Estonian national alleged to be a longstanding member of a prolific young English-speaking extortion crew was extradited from Finland to the US; the group has hit 100+ businesses and extorted over $100M since 2022. He faces conspiracy, cyber-intrusion and fraud charges.

incidents.victim: US life-sciences company (plus finance/HR/logistics staff globally)
incidents.vector: OAuth device-code phishing via vendor-impersonation invoice lures on look-alike SharePoint tenants captures tokens and Primary Refresh Tokens to bypass MFA and persist across password resets.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos uncovered 'ARToken', a mature business-email-compromise-as-a-service platform (80+ API endpoints, inbox-rule manipulation, seven-layer anti-analysis) sharing infrastructure with the EvilTokens operation; recovered lures spoofed a real Wisconsin contractor to target a US life-sciences firm's accounts-payable staff.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of an actively abused Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day as part of a broad extortion spree.
incidents.impact: Nissan North America disclosed a breach tied to the Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day campaign that has potentially infiltrated 100+ organizations, concentrated in higher education.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion; method undisclosed.
incidents.impact: The US insurance-sector standards body was breached and temporarily suspended insurer risk designations, prompting some credit-rating agencies to pause data sharing; NAIC says it has evicted the intruders and is restoring operations.

incidents.vector: Undisclosed intrusion and data theft.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole customer data from Aflac's Japanese branch affecting more than 4.38 million customers; the insurer had also disclosed a breach the prior June.

incidents.vector: A mix of attack types traced to Iranian military and IRGC units.
incidents.impact: Israel's National Cyber Directorate investigated 4,800 incidents in June 2026 versus 1,600 a year earlier — a roughly threefold rise in Iran-linked cyberattacks, most attributed to Iran's military and IRGC.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack disrupting the agency's website and email server.
incidents.impact: A cyberattack knocked the DC Housing Authority's website and email offline; the agency said this month's scheduled payments would not be affected.

incidents.victim: Transport for London; SSM Health and Sutter Health
incidents.vector: Help-desk social engineering and SIM-swapping to hijack corporate accounts.
incidents.impact: Two UK nationals (ages 20 and 18) pleaded guilty to the Aug 2024 Transport for London cyberattack; one also admitted hacking US healthcare providers SSM Health and Sutter Health. One defendant is tied to an indictment covering 120 intrusions, 47 US entities and $115M in ransoms.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion and data exfiltration; leaked after the victim declined to pay.
incidents.impact: Files allegedly taken from the Central Bank of Libya's network were published on the dark web by a ransomware group; Libyan authorities are investigating.

incidents.victim: US and allied government officials, military, journalists and Ukrainian officials
incidents.attacker: Russia — FSB and military intelligence services
incidents.vector: Phishing messages impersonating commercial messaging-app support to elicit verification codes, PINs and account backup-recovery keys, enabling account takeover.
incidents.impact: An FBI/CISA advisory warns of ongoing Russian intelligence targeting of high-value individuals' messaging accounts, exposing private and group message history; a stolen backup-recovery key can keep an account accessible even after it is re-created.

incidents.vector: Intrusion deploying novel ransomware with a previously unseen encryption algorithm and no ransom note.
incidents.impact: New reporting re-attributes the Aug–Oct 2025 Jaguar Land Rover hack — which halted production for over a month and, at roughly £1.9B economic impact, ranks as the UK's costliest cyberattack — to a Russian group rather than the Western teenagers who initially claimed it.

incidents.victim: Southeast Asian government and state-owned energy entities (10+ organizations)
incidents.vector: ASPX web shells on exploited web applications, then VPN tooling, credential dumpers, privilege-escalation utilities and a bespoke .NET backdoor for command execution, file exfiltration and screen capture.
incidents.impact: A Chinese-speaking espionage cluster exfiltrated web-server source code and a database from one government entity, ran reconnaissance on another, and breached two state-owned critical energy infrastructure entities, likely compromising 10+ organizations across late 2025.

incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion forcing a full IT-network shutdown.
incidents.impact: A newly emerged ransomware group demanded $2M from the Japanese motor and electronics maker, which took its entire IT network offline; the company was also hit by ransomware in late 2024.

incidents.victim: Major open-source projects (Linux kernel, FFmpeg, 7-Zip, PHP, OpenVPN, VLC and others)
incidents.vector: AI-assisted fuzzing to discover flaws, with proof-of-concept exploit code published without vendor notification.
incidents.impact: An anonymous researcher published working exploits and write-ups for 15+ zero-days across widely used open-source projects with no coordinated disclosure; at least nine have received CVEs and several vendors are rushing patches, with more drops promised.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion and data exfiltration; leaked after the victim refused to pay.
incidents.impact: A data-extortion group breached the Apple supplier and leaked roughly 200,000 documents — including images of the unreleased iPhone 18 and its components, plus alleged Apple and Tesla materials — after extortion demands were rejected.

incidents.victim: US Department of Homeland Security (Homeland Security Information Network)
incidents.vector: Intrusion targeting HSIN servers and a connected SharePoint system.
incidents.impact: Attackers breached DHS's Homeland Security Information Network — used to share sensitive information with federal, state, local and industry partners — between late May and early June; the intruders and any stolen data remain unknown.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion and data theft.
incidents.impact: A data-extortion group breached the US law firm in May; the firm declined to pay the ransom.
